draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Kannur! It's called the Land of Looms and Lore, thanks to its fabric industry and its many Theyyam temple festivals.
draft.hungryLine: Kannur eats Malabar style, biriyanis, puttu, appam and seafood, and look out for stuffed mussels, called arikkadukka, from local vendors.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Talap's Sundareshwara Temple is close by, and St. Angelo's Fort and Payyambalam Beach are a short drive.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: At Payyambalam Beach, sit in the little park and watch the sunset. The ticketed park is quieter than the sand.
moodReplies.surprise-me: In 2012 Diego Maradona showed off some magical moves with the ball at Kannur's Jawahar Municipal Stadium.

legends.title: A temple with no idol
legends.body: At the Muthappan Temple there's no idol. People worship through the Muttappan Theyyam ritual, and Muthappan is believed to be a form of Shiva.

tips.title: Go see a Theyyam.
tips.body: Theyyam temple festivals are a big part of Kannur life, and the Muthappan Temple holds regular performances.

tips.title: Head to Payyambalam at sunset.
tips.body: The park by the beach is the best seat in town for it.

story.title: Seat of Kolathunadu
story.body: Kannur was the headquarters of Kolathunadu, one of the four great dynasties of the Malabar Coast.

story.title: The Arakkal kingdom
story.body: The Arakkal kingdom held rights over Kannur city and the Laccadive Islands.

story.title: The Portuguese fort
story.body: The Portuguese built St. Angelo's Fort by the sea.

story.title: British capture
story.body: British forces under General Robert Abercromby besieged Cannanore and took it on 17 December 1790.

story.title: A municipality
story.body: Kannur municipality was formed on 1 November 1866.
